title: Right Before I Go is an important conversation starter ⭐️⭐️⭐️
transcript: Suicide is such a delicate topic and there are some rules for reporting on suicide that it is recommended to follow, including not publishing suicide notes. And so when I heard that there was a play here at the fringe that read aloud actual people suicide notes, I was nervous, definitely nervous. But I do think the intentions behind the play right before I go are well intentioned. And I do think they do a couple things that make me feel better about the show as a whole, including having a talk back at the end of the show with a mental health professional. Right before I go is a new play by Stan Zimmerman that not only contains the suicide notes, but also chronicles the journey that he took after losing his friend to suicide and some of the thought process that LED him down this path to want to do something about it. And that, that thing was this play. I do think the play itself is incredibly vulnerable. I don't necessarily know if the play in its form right now is doing exactly what it wants to do, though I do think that people are going to be more willing to talk about mental health issues upon leaving the play. And so in, in that sense, I do think overall it is a net positive. But there's something about the play itself and the way that it reads out these letters and the way that the narration. Happens that just feels very presentational as opposed to really hooking in the audience to these very real issues. The most fascinating piece for me was actually the story by the mental health professional at the end, the story of survival of what got him to that point and what ends ended up helping him out. Despite this being a subject matter that is very close to me, this just did not hit the emotional chords that I wanted to. That being said, I'm glad people are talking about it. I think it's an important subject to talk about, especially in referring to the shame that a lot of people have about out of this subject matter, whether you've attempted in your life or whether you know somebody who has died from it. If you would like to see right before I go, it is currently playing at Pleasant's Dome until the end of the fringe.
